THE HEADLINES:-

  1. 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to begin today in New Delhi; Prime Minister Narendra Modi to attend the event and meet leaders of visiting delegations.

  2. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar says, use of terrorism as instrument of statecraft is unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised.

  3. ISRO Chairman V Narayanan says, India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by 2029.

  4. Deep depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into Cyclonic Storm today.

  5. Brazil’s left-wing President Lula da Silva elected for fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro in knife-edge vote.

  6. And in Women’s Cricket, India beat Zimbabwe by 121 runs in second ODI to take unassailable 2-nil lead in three-match series.

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will commence in New Delhi from today. The theme of the two-day event is “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development.” Prime Minister Narendra Modi will grace the event and will meet the leaders of the visiting delegations. Eleven BRICS Member countries and 10 Partner countries have been invited for the event. Parliamentary delegations from these countries will participate in the meeting. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

         

 

 

“Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla will preside over the proceedings and hold discussions with leaders of the visiting delegations during the bilateral meetings. Building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th Forum aims to foster consensus-based dialogue through four High-Level Sessions based on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. A dedicated meeting of the Chairs of International Affairs Committees of Parliaments of BRICS Member and Partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity-building, and sharing of best practices. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, being hosted by India, will provide an opportunity to advance parliamentary diplomacy, strengthen democratic institutions, and promote cooperation among member and partner countries. Akshit Vedyan, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla today said that BRICS has evolved into an influential anchor of Global South and a driving force for multilateral architecture. In an article for a daily newspaper, Mr Birla said that the growing engagement among the BRICS countries has also strengthened its parliamentary dimension through the BRICS Parliamentary Forum.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that the use of terrorism as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised. He said, terrorism continues because not all states display zero tolerance for the menace. Dr Jaishankar was addressing an event held in New Delhi to mark 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. He said, the world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

 

 

 

         

 

 

He underlined the importance of peace, especially amid the ongoing conflicts in the world, and cautioned that war anywhere threatens peace everywhere. Dr Jaishankar cited the two major conflicts going on in the world, in Ukraine and in West Asia, and said societies and economies and people far away who have little say in the matter are actually paying the cost.

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

ISRO Chairman V Narayanan has said that India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by the year 2029. Mr. Narayanan said, these include a 2 thousand acre dedicated Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) complex at Kulasekarapattinam in Tuticorin district of Tamil Nadu and a third launch pad at Sriharikota, to meet the global demand for satellite launches. He was addressing convocation of a private university at Porur near Chennai.

 

 

 

         

 

 

The ISRO chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems.

 

 

         

 

Mr. Narayanan stated that ISRO plans to conduct the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within the next two months, followed by two subsequent uncrewed tests before the crewed mission.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will hold nationwide protests at all its state headquarters today against Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge for allegedly making derogatory remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Union Home Minister and Senior BJP Leader Amit Shah has hit out at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge over his alleged remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that this is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against the family of Prime Minister Modi. The Home Minister alleged that the leaders of Congress party have hurled insults at Mr Modi’s revered mother and mocked his poverty. He further alleged that the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi. Mr Shah said that the persistent electoral defeats over the last 12 years have led to such deep-seated frustration and despair within the Congress party.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti today. In a social media post, the President said that everyone effortlessly receives teachings on duty, good conduct, selfless action, the welfare of others, friendship, sacrifice, righteousness, and devotion from the epic Ramayana composed by Maharishi Valmiki.

 

 

         

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also extended his wishes to the citizens on the occasion. He said that the noble thoughts of Maharishi Valmiki have been the foundational elements of Indian culture and heritage, which will continue to nurture and flourish the nation in every era. Mr Modi added that Maharishi Valmiki’s invaluable messages for humanity will forever serve as guiding lights for the people of this country.

<><><> 

         

 

 

Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will be on a two day visit to Andhra Pradesh beginning today. During the visit, the Vice-President will attend the 40th Anniversary Celebrations of Dr NTR University of Health Sciences in Vijayawada as a chief guest.

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the Deep Depression over Bay of Bengal will intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm today. IMD has advised the fisherman not to venture into West central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.

 

 

Talking to Akashvani News, Director General of IMD, Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, due to influence of depression the sea condition is very rough and will deteriorate further. He said that the wind speed may lead to large scale damage of structures and standing crops. He said that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall may hit parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh during the next two days. Dr Mohapatra added that due to heavy rainfall can cause flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in hilly areas and urged the people living in these regions to be cautious. 

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

Odisha government has stepped up preparedness, deploying eight ministers to oversee arrangements in vulnerable districts as heavy rainfall and strong winds are forecast. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

 

 

 

“The India Meteorological Department has forecast that Cyclone Arnab will intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and a very severe cyclonic storm as it approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday. In Odisha, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has assigned eight ministers, including the two Deputy Chief Ministers, to oversee preparedness in Koraput, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Ganjam, Nabarangpur, Malkangiri, Kalahandi and Gajapati districts. Red warnings have been issued for all the southern districts for very heavy rainfall from tomorrow till Thursday. Some coastal districts will also experience very heavy rainfall under the impact of Cyclone Arnab. The state government has stepped up disaster-response arrangements, directed officials to remain alert and prioritised the safety of people in vulnerable areas. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

Our Visakhapatnam correspondent Satyanarayana has filed this report on weather condition in Andhra Pradesh:

 

 

“The Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts have been placed under an Orange Alert as a Deep Depression over the Eastcentral and Southeast Bay of Bengal rapidly intensifies into a major storm system. Landfall is expected by the forenoon of October 28, crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with destructive sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph. In anticipation of the cyclone’s impact, the IMD has warned of widespread heavy rainfall over the next two days and has urged the public to remain on high alert. Residents are strongly advised to postpone any travel plans, while fishermen have been strictly ordered not to venture into the sea. To counter the threat, the Andhra Pradesh state government is actively coordinating across all departments to deploy emergency resources, secure vulnerable areas, and prevent loss of life and property. Satyanarayana, Akashvani News, Visakhapatnam.”

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

 

In Brazil, Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s intense presidential race. With this victory, Lula has become the only politician in modern Brazilian history who successfully rebound and win the second round after falling behind in the first. A report:

 

 

         

 

 

“Incumbent Lula won the final runoff election with 51 percent of the vote and more than 51.49 million ballots. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro received 48.68 percent of the vote, which amounted to 48.8 million ballots. Just over 2.6 million votes separated the two candidates. Because of the close and highly contested race, voting stations across the country remained open two hours longer than originally planned.

         

 

 

The former metalworker union leader, at the age of 80 will be sworn into office on 5th of January next year, breaking his own record as the oldest president to take the oath of office since Brazil returned to a democracy. This victory marks an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term for Lula, who has run for the presidency a total of seven times. KAUMUDEE PAREEK FOR AKASHVANI NEWS DELHI.”

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

 

In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe by 121 runs in the second One Day International (ODI) in Vadodara last night, taking an unassailable 2-nil lead in the three-match series. Chasing a target of 329 runs, Zimbabwe were bowled out for 207 in 48.5 overs. Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano top scored with 46 runs off 57 balls. For India, Vaishnavi Sharma took four wickets, while Deepti Sharma claimed three.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

In Tennis, India’s top-ranked doubles player, Yuki Bhambri with his American partner Ryan Seggerman clinched the Almaty Open title in Kazakhstan yesterday. The fourth-seeded Indo-American pair defeated top seeds Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner of Austria 7-6, 6-7, 10-2 in the final of ATP 250 tournament.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) has announced that Ahmedabad will host the Senior World Weightlifting Championships in 2029. This will be the first time that India hosts the senior edition of the prestigious global event. The decision was taken at the IWF Executive Board meeting held in Ningbo, China.

 

 

AND NOW, FOR A LOOK AT TODAY’S NEWSPAPERS,

 

 

 

 

  • “Prime Ministar Modi watches ‘Wings over Ganga’ air show in Varanasi” leads The Statesman.

  • “PM Modi terms 12- year journey of Mann ki Baat as a ‘pilgrimage'” says The Asian Age.

  • Financial Express quotes PM Modi as saying “Must shield banks from cyber terrorists”.

  • “Milan to Tirana; Europe’s youth rise in anger” headlines The Pioneer. The paper says “Thousands march across major European cities as authorities deploy forces to prevent a repeat of last week’s violence”.

  • On the passing away of Jogen Chowdhury at the age of 87, Hindustan Times writes “Artist, teacher, acadmic, administrator; Man of many talents who left deep imprint on Indian art”.

  • And finally , “India beat Cameroon to make it two wins from two at FIFA U15 World Cup” reports The Statesman.
